drhp.business: SoftTech Engineers is an information technology and software services organisation delivering end-to-end solutions in the Architectural-Engineering-Construction (AEC) space through its Civit Suite of platforms, catering to government bodies, municipalities, property developers, investors, real estate companies, contractors, architects and consultants. The Company also provides specialist engineering services (BIM, AI, GIS, and implementation/professional services) that generate revenue in their own right and frequently serve as the entry point for a subsequent platform sale.
drhp.end_markets: Government bodies and urban local bodies (India)|Municipalities|Property developers, investors and real estate companies|Contractors and developers (private sector, via CivitBUILD)|Architects, small practices and individual professionals (via RuleBuddy PlanAssist)|Germany (AI Permit Twin deployment)|United States (stated FY 2026-27 productisation priority)|Middle East (traction established FY 2025-26, target of closing at least two major transactions in FY 2026-27)|Industrial and manufacturing sector (first material entry via Metawolf orders for CivitMETAVERSE)
drhp.expansion: Expansion during FY 2025-26 was platform and geography build-out rather than physical capacity: the Civit ecosystem was extended into transaction platforms (TDR), digital twins, artificial intelligence, immersive technologies and intelligent decision-support, producing new offerings including CivitTWIN, CivitTDRx, CivitMETAVERSE, CivitAI and BidAssist, which moved beyond product creation into real-world deployment — CivitTDRx went live with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) and CivitTWIN was launched with BMC. The NHEV national portal was launched and the Single Window Approval System for the EV ecosystem and Wayside Amenities was rolled out under the NHEV initiative. Internationally, eBGAI (a CivitTWIN variant for the German market) and a Ceramic Metaverse platform were conceptualised in Germany. Domestic footprint widened across Jharkhand, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. Horizon 3 of the strategic framework — expansion into high-value domestic and international markets via digital twin, AI and smart-infrastructure capabilities for airports, ports, highways and urban development — is intended to be executed in a capital-efficient manner, relying on strategic technology partnerships and partner-led go-to-market models rather than direct establishment of large overseas sales organisations. International operations moved from proof-of-concept to revenue generation during the year, with the Company now operating through subsidiaries in five countries in addition to its Indian base.

litigation.note: Company received income-tax reassessment notices under section 148A for AY 2018-19 (demand of Rs. 274.62 lakhs and separately Rs. 88.47 lakhs) and a GST short-payment demand for FY 2023-24; appeals filed to Commissioner (Appeals). Management states confidence that none of these contingent liabilities will result in material cash outflow. Read in the related-party/contingent-liabilities note of the Financial Statements section.

risks.note: Management calls this the Company's most material commercial exposure. Public-sector customers procure on extended timelines subject to budgetary and political cycles and pay on schedules the vendor does not control; days sales outstanding of 260 days quantifies the consequence. A high-interest-rate environment or fiscal consolidation reducing state/municipal capital expenditure would compress both new procurement and payment velocity.

Revenue is concentrated in a single customer type (government), a single geography (India) and a single regulatory domain (construction permitting). Each concentration is being actively reduced but remains a current structural exposure.

New entrants applying general-purpose AI to compliance workflows do not currently possess the regulatory dataset or deployment relationships the Company has accumulated, but improvements in general-purpose reasoning could reduce the value of holding a proprietary dataset.
The specialist combination the Company requires — engineers who understand both building regulation and machine learning — is scarce and is being bid for by better-capitalised employers.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for Civit Products is derived, forming in four stages: capital formation, regulatory events, a digitisation mandate, and platform procurement; construction volume becomes addressable revenue only where the digitisation mandate compels it, so policy rather than sector growth is the binding constraint.
- The segments the Company addresses are growing between 1.6 and 4.6 times faster than construction output, with the permitting layer procured by public authorities and following public budgets and reform mandates rather than the construction cycle.
- Once deployed, the permitting-layer system operates as a statutory record that is renewed rather than replaced, giving demand a different character from the rest of the market.
- Tier-two and tier-three Indian cities represent the largest volume of unpenetrated permitting authorities, are least able to fund discretionary technology from their own revenues, and are the tier targeted by the Urban Challenge Fund and its Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme; the constraint on converting them has been the Company's cost of entering each jurisdiction.
- Structural shift from licence to subscription as public authorities move from capital to operating budgets, with cloud already accounting for the majority of revenue in the global permitting software segment.
- Structural shift from grant-based to reform-linked funding: central funds are increasingly released against demonstrated governance and digital reform, shifting the Company's proposition from efficiency to eligibility — management regards this as the most durable of the demand drivers because it is embedded in the fiscal architecture rather than a time-bound mission.
- Consolidating procurement: tendering is moving from city-by-city to State-level and programme-level frameworks, favouring vendors able to demonstrate multi-jurisdiction deployment.
- An expanding compliance perimeter, with regulation extending from zoning, setbacks, fire and structure toward energy, embodied carbon, waste and water, enlarging the rule base.
- Authorities increasingly procuring integrated platform suites on shared data rather than point tools, favouring a single common architecture across products.
- Management's reading is that the current technology cycle favours incumbents holding a codified regulatory rule base and a statutory position inside public authorities, and disadvantages those without one.
- The National Infrastructure and Monetisation Pipelines sustain demand for CivitINFRA and linear-infrastructure twins, RERA raises the developer-side compliance burden supporting CivitPLAN, and Digital India remains the framework within which digital permitting procurement sits.
- CivitTWIN: deployed in Germany during the year; Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation issued a letter of intent for an AI Permit Twin deployment.
- CivitINFRA: deployed during the year for the Airports Authority of India and underlies the Delhi Development Authority's single-window clearance system; also deployed across J&K and Gujarat.
- CivitBUILD: Middle East traction established during FY 2025-26, with proof-of-concept activity in Oman.
- CivitTDRx: in service with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, serving more than 18,000 developers.
- CivitSUSTAIN: moved from research and development into order stage during FY 2025-26, with orders secured from Mitsubishi and a pipeline established at GIFT City.
- CivitMETAVERSE: moved from research and development to commercial order stage during the year with orders from Metawolf.
- CivitAI: growing pipeline for CivitAI and BIM-led services in the United States.
- RuleBuddy.ai: launched FY26 in Mumbai and Gujarat.
- Four platforms (CivitTWIN, CivitTDRx, CivitSUSTAIN, CivitMETAVERSE) advanced a stage of maturity during the year, a rate of commercialisation management describes as higher than previously achieved.

The NHEV national portal was launched and the Single Window Approval System for the EV ecosystem and Wayside Amenities was rolled out under the NHEV initiative. Internationally, eBGAI (a CivitTWIN variant for the German market) and a Ceramic Metaverse platform were conceptualised in Germany. Domestic footprint widened across Jharkhand, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. Horizon 3 of the strategic framework — expansion into high-value domestic and international markets via digital twin, AI and smart-infrastructure capabilities for airports, ports, highways and urban development — is intended to be executed in a capital-efficient manner, relying on strategic technology partnerships and partner-led go-to-market models rather than direct establishment of large overseas sales organisations. International operations moved from proof-of-concept to revenue generation during the year, with the Company now operating through subsidiaries in five countries in addition to its Indian base.

- customer lock-in: Once deployed, the permitting-layer system operates as a statutory record that is renewed rather than replaced — evidence: "once deployed the system operates as a statutory record that is renewed rather than replaced."

- Management calls this the Company's most material commercial exposure. Public-sector customers procure on extended timelines subject to budgetary and political cycles and pay on schedules the vendor does not control; days sales outstanding of 260 days quantifies the consequence. A high-interest-rate environment or fiscal consolidation reducing state/municipal capital expenditure would compress both new procurement and payment velocity.
- Revenue is concentrated in a single customer type (government), a single geography (India) and a single regulatory domain (construction permitting). Each concentration is being actively reduced but remains a current structural exposure.
- New entrants applying general-purpose AI to compliance workflows do not currently possess the regulatory dataset or deployment relationships the Company has accumulated, but improvements in general-purpose reasoning could reduce the value of holding a proprietary dataset.
- The specialist combination the Company requires — engineers who understand both building regulation and machine learning — is scarce and is being bid for by better-capitalised employers.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Platform-centric architecture: lifecycle management from planning through permitting, building and operations on a shared CivicCore data environment, where investment in the common layer benefits every product simultaneously.
- Recurring revenue focus: transition from one-time licensing to SaaS subscription, annual maintenance and pay-per-use transaction models, improving revenue predictability and shortening the collection cycle.
- Domain and technology fusion: combining three decades of AECO domain knowledge with artificial intelligence, geographic information systems and building information modelling.
- Global and local scalability: a modular rule engine adaptable to city, state and national regulation across jurisdictions, so entering a new market is a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild.
- Stakeholder integration: a single system serving governments, urban local bodies, contractors, architects, developers and citizens through different interfaces onto the same regulatory intelligence.
- Innovation beyond products: through AmpliNXT, the Company's corporate venture programme, SoftTech incubates next-generation technology start-ups in the AECO domain.
- Sustainability embedded rather than appended: through CivitSUSTAIN, sustainability and digital twin-based water and energy management are built into the core offering rather than sold as a separate module.
- Technology alignment through partnerships with Autodesk, Dassault, Esri, SAP, Microsoft and Mitsubishi, combined with local regulatory depth.
- International expansion designating Germany as the flagship international market, the United States for CivitTWIN/CivitAI productisation, the Middle East for CivitBUILD closures, and Asia-Pacific (Singapore, Malaysia) addressed through partner alliances such as CDCi.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
